claim.value: The reporting cutoff bounds the investigation without resolving the underlying uncertainty.
claim.scope: The effect of an administrative reporting boundary on investigation and knowledge.

provenance.rationale: The span explicitly distinguishes ending the investigation from resolving uncertainty and requires revision when later evidence arrives.

signal_basis.value: Set a reporting cutoff and stop active reconstruction at that boundary when applicability or the relevant sequence remains inadequately supported, reporting the case as unresolved with a follow-up owner and next step. Conflicts and missing links indicate continuing uncertainty.
signal_basis.scope: A case still unresolved at the reporting cutoff before the board review; these are proposed checks and possible findings, assumed to occur for this assessment.

provenance.rationale: The cited spans supply the reporting boundary, the stopping and unresolved-reporting procedure, the indicators of uncertainty, and their hypothetical status.
This supported claim requires no unresolved empirical relation to provide its warrant.

rationale: Stopping work at an administrative deadline supplies no evidence that resolves conflicting or missing links. The procedure expressly preserves unresolved cases and follow-up, licensing the distinction between a bounded investigation and continuing uncertainty.
uncertainty: The claim does not imply that every case remains unresolved; adequately supported cases may close earlier. Later evidence can change the account, as P032 specifies.
